newsitem.title: USA: U. S. stocks seen up as PPI soothes nerves.
newsitem.headline: U. S. stocks seen up as PPI soothes nerves.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open higher on Wednesday after October producer prices data showed inflation remains benign.
Analysts said the data heightened expectations that the Federal Reserve would hold monetary policy steady at its meeting later in the day.

Overall PPI rose 0.4 percent, higher than the expected 0.2 percent rise. But the core rate, excluding the volatile food and energy components, fell 0.3 percent, compared with an anticipated 0.1 percent rise.
The October core rate was the sharpest drop since the 0.4 percent decline in October 1994.

"The core is the key number. I have got to believe the market rallies on that. I would expect the Fed to take no action for both the November and December meetings. Inflation is not out there with this number," Philip Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management, said.
